text:
alex: Heads up — finance asked for a quick region-level comparison for next quarter commit planning. Can we summarize cost-per-GPU, expected latency delta, and any non-obvious egress/network charges?
maria: I can run a short sweep. high-level: SFO/ORD/AMS have different reserved discounts and spot availability. need a target QPS and seq len to be concrete. :point_up: cc @alex
jordan: Target = 200 8k-token requests/sec peak for inference fleet (mixed models). 95th p99 <= 150ms ideal for most routes.
lee: FYI ORD has cheaper reserved SKU pricing but higher cross-region latency for APAC failover. Also inter-AZ egress on some providers is non-negligible for our caching layer.
cost-bot: Quick numbers from billing (Q2 avg rates, per-GPU-hour):
```
SFO: on-demand $2.40/hr, reserved (1y) $1.76/hr (-27%), spot median $0.88/hr
ORD: on-demand $2.05/hr, reserved $1.44/hr (-30%), spot median $0.78/hr
AMS: on-demand $2.15/hr, reserved $1.55/hr (-28%), spot median $0.82/hr
```
maria: Thanks. Add network and egress multipliers: SFO egress to APAC +0.06/token-equivalent, ORD->EU egress cheaper by ~5%. Also consider regional SLA penalty risk for Dedicated.
alex: Can you map those to expected per-request cost for our 8k token average? even ballpark.
maria: Rough calc (tokens->GPU-hrs approximated by throughput sim):
```
Per-request token units: 8k tokens ~ 0.0022 GPU-hr (estimate)
SFO reserved: $1.76 * 0.0022 = $0.0039/request
ORD reserved: $1.44 * 0.0022 = $0.0032/request
AMS reserved: $1.55 * 0.0022 = $0.0034/request
Add network overhead: SFO +$0.0005, ORD +$0.0002, AMS +$0.0003
```
jordan: So ORD wins on unit cost. Is latency difference material? p95/p99?
sre-oncall: We ran a synthetic p99 run: SFO median = 110ms, p99 = 180ms; ORD median = 130ms, p99 = 220ms for same commit pack. AMS sits between. SFO better tail for US-west traffic (local zones).
lee: For APAC customers, APAC region (not in this list) still wins on latency even accounting for slightly higher per-unit cost. If we place too much in ORD, APAC traffic will pain on latency and egress.
alex: Ok. What's the incremental cost of using multi-region routing vs single-region with egress fallback?
maria: Multi-region: more reserved commitment (we'd need smaller slabs in each region) -> less discount efficiency. Example: splitting 10k GPUs across 3 regions raises effective blended reserved cost by ~4-7% vs concentrating in one region due to smaller purchase bands. Also cross-region cold KV fetches increase egress.
cost-bot: Simulation: concentrate 70% ORD, 20% SFO, 10% AMS vs 100% ORD:
```
70/20/10 blended reserved = $1.49/hr avg -> per-request ~$0.00327
100% ORD reserved = $1.44/hr -> per-request ~$0.00316
Delta = ~$0.00011/request (~3.5% increase) but p99 latency for US-west improves ~+30ms and APAC tail improves ~80-120ms depending on route.
```
jordan: For product, 30ms p99 improvement for US-west routes is noticeable for chat apps. APAC tail improvement might be required for enterprise customers.
